# Map authoring — building, terrain, batches and staging

Read this before your first `apply_architect_designator`, `jawa/set_terrain*` or
`jawa/spawn_batch` call. It is the detail behind §5 of the skill.

---

## Structure printing

**Structure printing works today.** A 13×11 furnished room took 21 calls and
~40 seconds: wall rects, a floor rect, a door, 4 beds, an end table, a dining
table with chairs, 2 lamps, a plant pot.

```python
put(WALL,  X,   Z,   W,   1)      # rectangles, not cells
put(FLOOR, X+1, Z+1, W-2, H-2)    # interior
put(DOOR,  X+6, Z)
```

Three things make it a real generator:

* `apply_architect_designator` takes **`width`/`height`**.
* **`dryRun: true`** validates without mutating. **Use it** — two workbenches
  failed because they were given corners with no clearance.
* **`flood_fill_cells` with a `designatorId`** is a *site finder*: every cell
  where that building legally fits, honouring footprint, anchor, walkability
  and pawn reachability.
* 🔑 **A `designatorId` is a UI path, not a defName** — `architect-designator:
  floors:build-concrete`, not `Floor_Concrete`. **Resolve it at runtime** by
  matching the trailing segment (`find_designator` in
  `src/RimMandrake/Utils/bridge_latency.py`); `list_architect_designators` needs
  a `categoryId` from `list_architect_categories` and returns dropdown parents
  beside leaves. **Never hardcode one** — ids carrying a positional index
  (`…-tutortagnotset-3`) renumber as mods add architect entries, so a path
  captured on the 3-mod tier is not safe at 568.

### 🔑 God mode is the other half of authoring — turn it on, then off

An Architect designator **queues work for a colonist**. On an authored or wiped
map there is nobody home, so `apply_architect_designator` returns `success: true`,
sets `designationCount: 1`, and changes nothing — the call is not lying, it did
designate. `rimworld/set_god_mode {"enabled": true}` converts designators to
instant effect and adds the fill/refuel button to refuelable things (there is no
refuel primitive on the bridge; in god mode it is a **button on the thing's
menu**). It also matters for `spawn_batch`, which places buildings **factionless**
— a `GravEngine` then shows `Claim` disabled and offers no Launch gizmo.

⚠️ **Turn it back off** (`{"enabled": false}`): left on, everything the owner
builds next is free and instant, and they save a god-mode map without knowing.
⚠️ **A cell that already carries a designation refuses a second one**
(`success: false`) — cancel first with the category's `…-cancel` designator.

📌 Before concluding "the bridge cannot do X", ask what the UI would do with the
same click: the answer is often "X needs a worker and there is nobody home".

### 🔴 The build order is foundation → terrain → things, and it is the only one

`SetFoundation` is **refused on any cell that already carries a floor, silently
at the write** — `jawa/set_terrain_batch layer='foundation'` reported
`cellsChanged: 16` with `cellsFailedVerify: 12` on the 12 cells that had a floor.
Controlled three ways: bare ground 25/0/25 hold; `MetalTile` first
25/**25 failedVerify**/0; foundation then floor 25/0/25, surviving the floor.
**There is no retrofit** — a floor is a one-way door, recoverable only by
demolish-and-rebuild and undetectable by inspection afterwards. Only the
read-back catches it.

⚠️ **Affordance does not gate spawning.** `GravshipHull` declares
`terrainAffordanceNeeded=Substructure` and spawns happily on bare ground, because
`jawa/spawn_batch` routes through `GenSpawn`, which checks no affordance —
affordance constrains the *designator*. A substructure-less ship is buildable and
**not a gravship**, which is worse, because everything looks right.

### 🔑 Multi-cell things spawn CENTRED on the cell you name

`GenAdj.OccupiedRect` computes `minX = loc.x - (w-1)/2`, so `GravEngine:172,172`
— a 3×3 — occupies x/z **171–173**. Emit **centres** in any `Def:x,z` op grammar,
and test coordinate semantics with the **largest** thing you have, never the most
common one: 1×1 things read identically under both conventions, so a plan that is
95% single-cell looks perfect while every large thing places wrong.

### ⏳ Assert after time has run, not at tick 0

A tool-built thing arrives in a state no played thing is ever in: every cached
comp value is cold and several refresh only on their own tick. A `ChemfuelTank`
filled by hand on a **paused** map still failed the launch check for "not enough
fuel" — the thrusters had not registered it. `ticksGame: 1` on every read-back is
the tell that you are asserting before the game has had a chance to disagree.
**Do not treat a refusal on a paused, just-built object as a defect** — run time
briefly and re-read.

### 🔑 Laying a floor destroys what is under it

The most useful discovery for map authoring. A floor rectangle wipes grass,
bushes and plants inside it. This is the **indirect destruction primitive** —
there is no working direct one.

def save_site(call, name, saves_dir, wait_s=180, sleep=time.sleep):
    """save_game under `name`, then STAT: a new <name>.rws appeared and no existing file changed (save_game has
    written the CURRENT slot instead of saveName before). Never overwrites: a rebuilt site takes the next _vN."""
    before = saves_stat(saves_dir)
    if name + ".rws" in before:
        raise RuntimeError("%s.rws already exists -- a site save is never overwritten; build the next version" % name)
    call("rimworld/save_game", saveName=name)
    t0 = time.time()
    while name + ".rws" not in saves_stat(saves_dir):
        if time.time() - t0 > wait_s:
            raise RuntimeError("no %s.rws appeared in %s within %ds" % (name, saves_dir, wait_s))
        sleep(POLL_S)
    sleep(3.0)                                  # the writer finishes the file after it appears
    after = saves_stat(saves_dir)
    touched = [f for f in before if after.get(f) != before[f]]
    if touched:
        raise RuntimeError("save touched existing file(s) %s" % touched)
    # Every builder saves here, so no fixture leaves holding the list-bound compressed grid (save_uncompress.py).
    path = os.path.join(saves_dir, name + ".rws")
    expanded = save_uncompress.expand_fresh(path)
    return {"path": path, "bytes": expanded["bytes"], "expanded": expanded}


def _state(call):
    try:
        return (call("rimworld/get_ui_state") or {}).get("programState")
    except Exception:                            # noqa: BLE001 - the bridge drops calls during a load
        return None


def _wait(pred, budget_s, sleep):
    t0 = time.time()
    while time.time() - t0 < budget_s:
        try:
            if pred():
                return round(time.time() - t0, 1)
        except Exception:                        # noqa: BLE001
            pass
        sleep(POLL_S)
    return None

def _journal_seq(call):
    """The bridge journal's latest sequence number (0 when unreadable)."""
    try:
        lg = call("rimbridge/list_logs", limit=1, minimumLevel="trace") or {}
        return max([int(x.get("Sequence", 0)) for x in lg.get("logs") or []] or [0])
    except Exception:              # noqa: BLE001 - a missing baseline only widens the scan
        return 0

# HugeFootprints performance: the code, the 70 ms/tick issue, the fix, and alternatives

Written 2026-10-10 (FOUNDRY, offline). Durable companion to `design/RimMandrake/giant_footprint_design_2026-10-07.md`
(what the feature is) and the brief for a GPT deep dive on alternative algorithms (§6).

**Owner ruling, 2026-10-10:** the Rot's density (2,811 footprint giants on a 250x250 map, ~7,400 trunk blockers,
~12% of cells, ~1,315 refused claims) **is intended and acceptable. The cost must be handled in code.** Nothing here
proposes thinning the roster or the biome's `plantDensity`.

Evidence labels: **MEASURED** (a number from a live run, with its source), **READ-FROM-CODE** (read in the source at
the cited line, at commit `f3774dd15`), **UNVERIFIED** (reasoning or an engine claim nobody has checked; a hypothesis
to test, never a fact to repeat).

Source paths (all under `src/RimMandrake/HugeThings/Source/`):

| file | holds |
|---|---|
| `MapComponent_HugeFootprints.cs` | the per-map component: claims, pending cells, realize, relabel, reconcile |
| `CompHugeFootprint.cs` | per-plant comp: signature, desired cells, planning window |
| `Kernel/RM_HugeClaimsKernel.cs` | Verse-free `ClaimLedger`, `Planner`, `ItemMover`, `FootprintSignature` |
| `Kernel/RM_HugeFootprintKernel.cs` | Verse-free draw transform and contact-cell geometry |
| `Building_TrunkBlocker.cs` | the invisible impassable edifice per blocked cell |
| `HugeThingsCore.cs` | opt-in, Harmony patches (`Plant.TickLong`, `PlantCollected`, zones, explosions, gravship) |
| `../Defs/ThingDefs/RM_HugeTrunkBlocker.xml` | the blocker def |
| `src/RimMandrake/TheRot/Patches/RotGiants_HugeFootprint.xml` | generated per-species contact masks |

## 1. The feature, data model, lifecycle, old and new algorithm

### 1.1 What it is for

The Rot draws several fungi up to 20 cells wide, but RimWorld has no multi-cell plant: each is a one-cell `Plant`.
Owner ruling 2026-10-07 (option 1, then the rework card at 20:05): *"Solid trunk, open canopy"*; the selection rect
wraps the whole drawn picture; **pawns are blocked wherever the art touches the ground**, measured from the art,
never under the cap. Mechanism (design doc §Mechanism): each blocked cell gets one invisible impassable edifice
`RM_HugeTrunkBlocker`, so vanilla's path grid, regions, blueprint placement and sowing all treat it as solid with no
patches. Trunk cells give partial cover (`fillPercent` 0.4) and forward hits to the plant.

Why Things and not a path-cost patch (design doc §"Why not the alternatives", READ-FROM-CODE of the doc, engine
claims there are UNVERIFIED here): a cost patch would not refuse buildings or stop plants, and `Plant` cannot be
`size > 1`.

        matches = r.rec['running'].get('assembly', {}).get('matches', [])
        require(len(matches) == 1 and matches[0].get('sha256') == sha(dll), 'loaded DLL differs from this clone')

        quiet = H.quiet_world(T.call_session(r.call), tx, wild_spawner=False, log_raids=False)
        require(quiet.verified, 'quiet controls unreadable')
        r.rec['quiet'] = quiet.evidence
        r.scenario(tx)
        r.rec['ok'] = True
    except Exception as exc:
        r.rec['error'] = repr(exc)
    finally:
        errors = []
        if saved:
            try:
                r.rec['restore_load'] = T.load_site(r.call, 'calm', name=snapshot, check=False, map_controls=('modal_broker',))
                require(r.rec['restore_load']['verified'], 'scene-begin restoration load failed')
                restored = r.sc('Rect', RECT, PROOF)
                restored_pawns = r.pawns()
                r.rec['restored'] = dict(rectangle=restored, pawns=restored_pawns)
                require(restored == baseline and restored_pawns == baseline_pawns, 'restored rectangle/fixtures differ from exact baseline')
            except Exception as exc:
                errors.append(repr(exc))
        for field, value in r.prior.items():
            try:
                r.setting(field, value)
                require(r.field(field) == value, 'exact setting restoration mismatch '+field)
            except Exception as exc:
                errors.append(repr(exc))
        if tx:
            try:
                tx.__exit__(None, None, None)
            except Exception as exc:
                errors.append(repr(exc))
        for pid in r.rec['fixture_ids']:
            C.withdraw_fixture(pid)
        r.rec['restoration'] = dict(ok=saved and not errors, errors=errors, settings=dict(r.prior))
        r.rec['ok'] = r.rec['ok'] and r.rec['restoration']['ok']
        r.rec['finished'] = time.time()
        r.persist()
        print('PASS' if r.rec['ok'] else 'FAIL', r.rec.get('error', ''), errors, flush=True)
    return 0 if r.rec['ok'] else 1


if __name__ == '__main__':

            self.prior[field] = self.field(field)
        self.call('jawa/mod_settings_field', typeName=SETTINGS, field=field, action='set', value=str(value))
        require(self.field(field).lower() == str(value).lower(), 'setting did not stick '+field)

    def ticks(self, count):
        start = self.call('jawa/site_state')['ticksGame']
        executed = C.advance_chunk(T.call_session(self.call), count)
        end = self.call('jawa/site_state')['ticksGame']
        require(executed == count and end-start == count, 'governor tick delta differs')

    def things(self, defname=None, rect=RECT):
        args = dict(rect=rect, limit=5000)
        if defname:
            args['defName'] = defname
        result = self.call('jawa/list_things', **args)
        require(result.get('isCompleteList') is True and result.get('countMatched') == len(result.get('things', [])), 'incomplete thing census')
        return result['things']

    def pawns(self, rect=RECT):
        result = self.call('jawa/list_pawns', rect=rect, limit=1000)
        require(result.get('truncated') == 0 and result.get('returned') == len(result.get('pawns', [])), 'incomplete pawn census')
        return result['pawns']

    def reach(self, pawn, x, z):
        result = self.call('jawa/order_pawn', allow=True, pawnId=pawn, x=x, z=z, pathEndMode='oncell',
                           waitTicks=0, unpause=False, draft=True)
        self.call('jawa/stop_job', pawnId=pawn, mode='stopall')
        rows = result.get('pawns', [])
        require(len(rows) == 1 and result.get('ticksElapsed') == 0 and rows[0]['start'] == rows[0]['end'], 'invalid paused path read')
        require(type(rows[0].get('canReach')) is bool, 'path answer missing')
        return rows[0]['canReach']

    def spawn_pawn(self, x, z):
        rows = self.call('jawa/spawn_pawn', kindDef='Colonist', x=x, z=z, faction='player', count=1, xenotype='Baseliner')['pawns']
        require(len(rows) == 1, 'wrong spawn cardinality')
        pid = rows[0]['id']
        self.rec['fixture_ids'].append(pid)
        C.declare_fixture(pid)
        self.call('jawa/set_draft', pawnId=pid, drafted=True)
        return pid

    def stage_plant(self, x, z, growth=0.2499):
        result = self.call('jawa/artboard_stage', phase='subjects', pause=True, killHostiles=False,
                           ops='id=plant|kind=plant|x=%d|z=%d|def=%s|growth=%.7f' % (x, z, PLANT, growth))
        rows = result.get('ops', [])
        require(len(rows) == 1 and rows[0].get('ok') and abs(float(rows[0]['readBack']['growth'])-growth) < 0.000001, 'plant initial growth not staged exactly')
        plants = self.things(PLANT, '%d,%d,1,1' % (x, z))
        require(len(plants) == 1, 'plant identity missing')
        return plants[0]['id']

    def identity(self, tid):
        rows = [t for t in self.things() if t['id'] == tid]
        require(len(rows) == 1, 'lost Thing '+tid)
        return rows[0]

    def scenario(self, tx):
        require(not self.pawns(), 'SITE: target rectangle already contains pawns; refuse clearing')
        self.call('jawa/set_roof_batch', ops='None:'+RECT)
        self.call('jawa/destroy_batch', categories='All', rects=RECT)
        require(not self.things(), 'SITE: bounded clear left objects')
        self.call('jawa/set_terrain_batch', ops='Soil:'+RECT)
        for field, value in dict(giantPlantsEnabled=True, plantTrunkEnabled=True, plantTrunkScale=1, plantItemPushEnabled=False).items():
            self.setting(field, value)
        self.sc('RefreshAllMaps')
        # A real workshop with one southern door. The root outside is surrounded
        # on the other seven adjacent cells by existing walls; its only open touch
        # cell is the doorway approach, which is genuine Nogtyl contact after growth.
        walls = {(x, z) for x in range(95, 106) for z in (102, 111)} | {(x, z) for x in (95, 105) for z in range(103, 111)}
        walls.remove((100, 102))
        walls |= {(99, 99), (100, 99), (101, 99), (99, 100), (101, 100), (99, 101), (101, 101)}
        self.call('jawa/build_batch', ops=';'.join('Wall:%d,%d' % p for p in sorted(walls)), stuff='WoodLog', faction='player')
        self.call('jawa/build_batch', ops='Door:100,102;TableStonecutter:98,108', stuff='WoodLog', faction='player')
        door = self.things('Door', '100,102,1,1')
        bench = self.things('TableStonecutter', '96,106,5,5')
        require(len(door) == len(bench) == 1, 'workshop door/bench not built')
        self.rec['door_before'], self.rec['bench_before'] = door[0], bench[0]
        cutter = self.spawn_pawn(100, 107)
        self.rec['cutter'] = cutter
        self.call('jawa/set_work_priority', pawnId=cutter, workType='PlantCutting', priority=1)
        require(self.reach(cutter, 100, 97), 'SITE: workshop already inaccessible')
        plant = self.stage_plant(100, 100)
        self.rec['plant_id'] = plant
        young = self.sc('DebugPlantState', 'current|100,100')
        require(kv(young).get('oldEnough') == 'False' and kv(young).get('desired') == '0', 'not a young unblocked baseline')
        require(not self.things(BLOCKER, '96,96,9,6') and self.reach(cutter, 100, 97), 'young plant already seals access')
        self.rec['young_state'] = young
        samples = []
        for _ in range(6):
            self.ticks(2000)
            state = self.sc('DebugPlantState', 'current|100,100')
            samples.append(dict(state=state, things=self.things(BLOCKER, '96,96,9,6')))
            if kv(state).get('oldEnough') == 'True' and int(kv(state).get('claimed', 0)) > 0:
                break
        self.rec['growth_samples'] = samples
        require(samples and kv(samples[-1]['state']).get('oldEnough') == 'True', 'SITE: plant did not naturally cross growth threshold')
        require(float(kv(samples[-1]['state'])['growth']) > 0.2499, 'no measured natural growth')
        self.ticks(500)
        blockers = self.things(BLOCKER, '100,101,1,1')
        sealed = not self.reach(cutter, 100, 97)
        self.rec['sealed'] = dict(blockers=blockers, access=not sealed, state=self.sc('DebugPlantState', 'current|100,100'))
        require(sealed and len(blockers) == 1, 'MOD: growth did not seal workshop doorway (old access-preserving behavior)')
        require(self.identity(door[0]['id']) == door[0], 'growth changed door identity/HP')
        # Standard root work is explicitly unable to reach it. The replacement
        # giver must permit touching this owned blocker, not silently leave a gap.
        self.call('jawa/designate_batch', action='add', designation='CutPlant', rect='100,100,1,1')
        root_probe = self.call('jawa/workgiver_probe', pawn=cutter, thing=plant, workGiver='CutPlants')
        require(root_probe['gates']['canReachTouchDeadly'] is False, 'root was deliberately left reachable')
        probe = self.call('jawa/workgiver_probe', pawn=cutter, thing=blockers[0]['id'], workGiver=CUT)
        self.rec['cut_probes'] = dict(root=root_probe, trunk=probe)
        require(probe['gates']['canReach'] is True and probe['gates']['canReserve'] is True and probe.get('job', {}).get('def') == CUT,
                'trunk cutting giver did not produce a reachable/reservable real job')
        self.call('jawa/set_draft', pawnId=cutter, drafted=False)
        self.call('jawa/stop_job', pawnId=cutter, mode='stopall')
        ordered = self.call('jawa/prioritized_work', pawnId=cutter, jobDef=CUT, workGiverDef=CUT,
                            targetAId=plant, targetBId=blockers[0]['id'], waitTicks=0)
        require(ordered.get('accepted') is True and ordered.get('nowRunningRequested') is True, 'cut order was queued but not running')
        self.ticks(20)
        require(any(t['id'] == plant for t in self.things(PLANT)), 'cut completed without measured work interval')
        occupied = 'CODEX_TrunkDoors_Cutting_'+uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]
        self.rec['cut_save'] = T.save_site(self.call, occupied, G.SAVES)
        self.rec['cut_reload'] = T.load_site(self.call, 'calm', name=occupied, check=False, map_controls=('modal_broker',))
        require(self.rec['cut_reload']['verified'], 'cutting snapshot did not reload')
        H.quiet_world(T.call_session(self.call), tx, wild_spawner=False, log_raids=False)
        self.rec['cut_job_after_reload'] = self.pawns()
        for _ in range(30):
            self.ticks(100)
            if not any(t['id'] == plant for t in self.things(PLANT)):
                break
        require(not any(t['id'] == plant for t in self.things(PLANT)), 'actual cutting job never removed enclosed plant')
        self.call('jawa/set_draft', pawnId=cutter, drafted=True)
        self.ticks(500)
        require(not self.things(BLOCKER, '96,96,9,6'), 'plant blockers survived cutting/cleanup')
        require(self.reach(cutter, 100, 97), 'access not restored after real cutting')
        require(self.identity(door[0]['id']) == door[0] and self.identity(bench[0]['id']) == bench[0], 'cutting altered door/workshop')
        self.rec['cut_recovered'] = True
        self.controls()

    def controls(self):
        # Each plant has positive free contact cells as well as the obstructed
        # one: an absent/disabled footprint cannot satisfy placement protection.
        guard = self.spawn_pawn(125, 101)
        self.call('jawa/spawn_batch', ops='Steel:140,101,17')
        item = self.things('Steel', '140,101,1,1')
        require(len(item) == 1, 'item control absent')
        self.call('jawa/build_batch', ops='Door:155,101', stuff='WoodLog', faction='player')
        door = self.things('Door', '155,101,1,1')
        require(len(door) == 1, 'protected building control absent')
        for x in (125, 140, 155, 175):
            self.stage_plant(x, 100)
        self.ticks(2000)
        self.ticks(500)
        for x in (125, 140, 155):
            require(not self.things(BLOCKER, '%d,101,1,1' % x), 'placement control was overwritten')
            require(self.things(BLOCKER, '%d,98,7,6' % (x-3)), 'obstruction control has no positive free-space blocker')
        require(self.identity(item[0]['id']) == item[0], 'item moved/wiped with item push disabled')
        require(self.identity(door[0]['id']) == door[0], 'existing building wiped/changed')
        pawn_rows = [p for p in self.pawns() if p['id'] == guard]
        require(len(pawn_rows) == 1 and pawn_rows[0]['x'] == 125 and pawn_rows[0]['z'] == 101 and not pawn_rows[0].get('dead') and not pawn_rows[0].get('downed'), 'pawn placement control moved/hurt')
        free_before = self.things(BLOCKER, '172,98,7,6')
        require(free_before, 'free-space positive has no blockers')
        self.setting('plantTrunkEnabled', False)
        self.sc('RefreshAllMaps')
        self.ticks(500)
        require(not self.things(BLOCKER), 'disabled trunk feature left blockers')
        self.setting('plantTrunkEnabled', True)
        self.sc('RefreshAllMaps')
        self.ticks(500)
        require(self.things(BLOCKER, '172,98,7,6'), 'reenabled free-space feature did not resume')
        self.rec['controls'] = dict(pawn=guard, item=item[0], building=door[0], free_before=free_before,
                                    disabled=True, reenabled=True)


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument('--out', type=Path, required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    args.out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    r = Run(args.out)
    snapshot = 'CODEX_TrunkDoors_Begin_'+uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]
    saved = False
    baseline = baseline_pawns = None
    tx = None
    try:
        dll = HERE.parent/'Assemblies/RM_HugeThings.dll'
        r.rec['assembly_sha256'] = sha(dll)
        r.rec['running'] = r.call('jawa/running_mods', assemblyName='RM_HugeThings')
        matches = r.rec['running'].get('assembly', {}).get('matches', [])
        require(len(matches) == 1 and matches[0].get('sha256') == sha(dll), 'loaded DLL differs from this clone')
        name = T.read_registry().get('calm', {}).get('save') or T.SITES['calm']['save']
        require(name.startswith('RM_TestSite_') and (Path(G.SAVES)/(name+'.rws')).is_file(), 'existing registered site missing')
        r.rec['site_load'] = T.load_site(r.call, 'calm', name=name, map_controls=('modal_broker',))
        require(r.rec['site_load']['verified'], 'SITE: registered site did not load')
        r.rec['snapshot'] = T.save_site(r.call, snapshot, G.SAVES)
        saved = True
        r.rec['baseline_load'] = T.load_site(r.call, 'calm', name=snapshot, check=False, map_controls=('modal_broker',))
        require(r.rec['baseline_load']['verified'], 'scene-begin reload failed')
        baseline = r.sc('Rect', RECT, PROOF)
        baseline_pawns = r.pawns()
        r.rec['baseline'] = dict(rectangle=baseline, pawns=baseline_pawns)
        tx = H.SettingsTransaction(T.call_session(r.call)); tx.__enter__()
        quiet = H.quiet_world(T.call_session(r.call), tx, wild_spawner=False, log_raids=False)
        require(quiet.verified, 'quiet controls unreadable')
        r.rec['quiet'] = quiet.evidence
        r.scenario(tx)
        r.rec['ok'] = True
    except Exception as exc:
        r.rec['error'] = repr(exc)
    finally:
        errors = []
        if saved:
            try:
                r.rec['restore_load'] = T.load_site(r.call, 'calm', name=snapshot, check=False, map_controls=('modal_broker',))
                require(r.rec['restore_load']['verified'], 'scene-begin restoration load failed')
                restored = r.sc('Rect', RECT, PROOF)
                restored_pawns = r.pawns()
                r.rec['restored'] = dict(rectangle=restored, pawns=restored_pawns)
                require(restored == baseline and restored_pawns == baseline_pawns, 'restored rectangle/fixtures differ from exact baseline')
            except Exception as exc:
                errors.append(repr(exc))
        for field, value in r.prior.items():
            try:
                r.setting(field, value)
                require(r.field(field) == value, 'exact setting restoration mismatch '+field)
            except Exception as exc:
                errors.append(repr(exc))
        if tx:
            try:
                tx.__exit__(None, None, None)
            except Exception as exc:
                errors.append(repr(exc))
        for pid in r.rec['fixture_ids']:
            C.withdraw_fixture(pid)
        r.rec['restoration'] = dict(ok=saved and not errors, errors=errors, settings=dict(r.prior))
        r.rec['ok'] = r.rec['ok'] and r.rec['restoration']['ok']
        r.rec['finished'] = time.time()
        r.persist()
        print('PASS' if r.rec['ok'] else 'FAIL', r.rec.get('error', ''), errors, flush=True)
    return 0 if r.rec['ok'] else 1


if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(main())

design2 # Verdict: sound, if five specific gaps are closed

The proposed reuse is the smallest sound route. A custom driver would duplicate the whole cutting pipeline: the queue/ideology validator toils, the `WorkDonePerTick` formula (the IL you measured), harvestWork accounting, skill learning, effecter and sound, yield placement, `PlantCollected`, history events and `DestroyThing(B)` with PlantCut mode. Every one of those would then drift silently, both from vanilla and from other mods' patches to `JobDriver_PlantWork`. You could call the public static `WorkDonePerTick`, but the remaining collection and destroy logic still has to be copied. Redirecting exactly two target indices in one iterator keeps a much smaller semantic surface. It is also smaller than patching reach globally (making `CanReach` or `CanReachImmediate(plant, Touch)` succeed via blockers), which would affect every job in the game.

The five gaps below are each concrete enough to break the design as described.

## 1. The wrappers have no job context unless you inject it

`Toils_Goto.GotoThing(TargetIndex, PathEndMode, bool)` and `ToilFailConditions.FailOnCannotTouch<T>(T, TargetIndex, PathEndMode)` are static. A same-signature wrapper cannot know which JobDef it is building for. `GotoThing` also captures `ind` at construction, so you cannot defer the choice to the toil's runtime `actor`.

The transpiler must load the driver before each call: `ldarg.0; ldfld <>4__this`. It then calls wrappers shaped like this:

- `GotoThingRH(TargetIndex ind, PathEndMode pe, bool parent, JobDriver d)`
- `FailOnCannotTouchRH(Toil f, TargetIndex ind, PathEndMode pe, JobDriver d)`

Note that `FailOnCannotTouch` is a closed generic `<Toil>`, so you match that exact instantiation.

Deciding at construction time is valid because a driver is bound to one Job and `MakeNewToils` runs once per driver, including again after load. The redirect predicate is: `d.job.def == RM_CutHugePlantViaBlocker && d.job.targetC.HasThing`. Otherwise the wrapper passes `ind` through untouched.

## 2. Validate the transpiler match and fail closed

The match must find exactly one `GotoThing` call and exactly one `FailOnCannotTouch<Toil>` call in `JobDriver_PlantWork`'s `MakeNewToils` `MoveNext`. Each must be immediately preceded by the literal constants for (`TargetIndex.B`, `PathEndMode.Touch`, `false`) and (`TargetIndex.B`, `PathEndMode.Touch`) respectively.

If the counts or operands differ (another version, or another mod's transpiler), do three things:

- Apply nothing.
- Log once.
- Disable the blocker WorkGiver (`ShouldSkip` returns true) and refuse to issue the JobDef.

Without that last step, a failed patch would issue jobs whose vanilla `GotoThing(B)` targets an unreachable root. That causes pather failures and, through the repeated failures, the "too many jobs in one tick" loop error.

## 3. Constrain what vanilla `JobOnThing` returns

Calling the vanilla `WorkGiver_PlantsCut` worker instance (from its WorkGiverDef, not a new instance) on the plant is correct. It preserves CanReserve, ideology willingness, PreventCutting, burning and forced semantics. It bypasses reach only because the scanner's reach check runs against the blocker, which is what you want.

Do not trust its result shape, though. Accept the result only if all of these hold:

- `job.def == JobDefOf.CutPlant`. It returns HarvestDesignated for harvest designations, which is out of scope.
- `targetA.Thing == plant`.
- The target queues are empty.

If you don't reject queued targets, `ExtractNextTargetFromQueue` changes A/B mid-job while C still points at the first plant's blocker.

Reuse beats a copied driver. The cut toil's tick body includes work rate, skill XP, yield placement and failure chance, `PlantCollected`, records and DLC hooks. A copy of that body drifts silently across versions and DLCs. The transpiler can be made to fail closed. A copied driver cannot detect its own drift.

I found no design flaw. There is one input inconsistency and several implementation details where the design could go wrong.

## Input inconsistency to resolve first

The brief says "all plant/reservation/designation/work/yield code uses A", but it also says the engine calls **`DestroyThing(B)`**. In vanilla, B is empty for cut jobs, so `Toils_Interact.DestroyThing` on B would throw on a null target. This is almost certainly another index-decoding error, and the operand is really A (`ldc.i4.1`).

- Re-read the `PlantWorkDoneToil` operand on `JobDriver_PlantCut` against the installed enum before writing the transpiler validator.
- Either way, **never put anything in B.** Using C for the blocker remains correct.

## Required implementation conditions

### 1. The wrappers need the driver instance
`GotoThing(TargetIndex, PathEndMode, bool)` and `FailOnCannotTouch` cannot see the job.

- The transpiler must inject `ldarg.0; ldfld <>4__this` (the iterator's captured driver) as an extra wrapper argument.
- Resolve that field by reflection. If it is not exactly one field of type `JobDriver_PlantWork`, abort the patch.

### 2. The wrappers run when the toils are built, so runtime checks go on the toil
`MakeNewToils` is enumerated once at job start and again on load. Choosing C there is a one-time decision.

- The ongoing checks must be added as fail conditions **on that toil**:
  - C is still spawned and realized.
  - The claim owner set of C contains the *current* `job.targetA`.
  - C is on the same map.
  - The setting is active.
- Do not use driver-level `this.FailOn` (global fail conditions). `PlantCollected` despawns the blockers within the completing tick. A global condition would then mark a successful cut as Incompletable and skip the designation-removal toil.

### 3. Both branches must yield the same toils
- Each wrapper returns exactly one toil, whether it takes the C branch or the vanilla branch.
- `curToilIndex` is restored by index on load, so the toil count and order must not depend on whether C is valid.
- If C is invalid at build time (for example after a load), still build the C-targeted toil and let its fail condition end the job. Never fall back to A mid-job.

### 4. Transpiler matching must be exact and fail closed
- Match the exact 3-argument `Toils_Goto.GotoThing` overload.
- Match `ToilFailConditions.FailOnCannotTouch<Toil>` by generic method definition plus the `Toil` type argument. The wrapper is non-generic, takes `Toil` and returns `Toil`, so the stack shape is unchanged.
- Require exactly one of each call in `MoveNext`.
- Each call must be preceded by a constant equal to `(int)TargetIndex.A` and `(int)PathEndMode.Touch`, both read at runtime. Do not hard-code these from memory, given the earlier decoding error.
- On any mismatch, including IL already altered by another mod's transpiler:
  - patch nothing;
  - log once;
  - make the new WorkGiver return null.
- Vanilla behaviour must be unchanged in that case.

### 5. The wrapper selects C only when every one of these holds
- `job.def` is the new JobDef, and the driver is a `JobDriver_PlantCut_Designated`.
- `job.targetC` is valid, and the claim owner set of C contains `targetA`.
- Use the *same* shared-owner predicate that the WorkGiver used, not a primary-owner check. Otherwise nonprimary-plant cuts pass the WorkGiver and then fail the wrapper.
- `targetQueueA` is empty when the job is created. Your WorkGiver never queues. If anything else does, the owner check from condition 2 ends the job safely.

### 6. WorkGiver details
- Vanilla `WorkGiver_PlantsCut.JobOnThing` returns **`HarvestDesignated`** when the plant has a harvest designation. Accept its result only if `def == CutPlantDesignated`. Then build the new job, copying the `forced` flag.
- Vanilla `JobOnThing` already checks `t.IsForbidden(pawn)` on the plant. That check includes **area restriction at the root cell**. This is conservative and acceptable, but document it and test it.
- The scanner framework checks reachability and forbidden status on the scanned blocker. Set `PathEndMode = Touch`.
- Set `priorityInType` below vanilla PlantsCut so that a reachable root still goes through vanilla.
- `ShouldSkip` when no huge plant carries a CutPlant designation.
- Copy the relevant JobDef fields from CutPlantDesignated: report string, suspendable, casual-interruptible, `allowOpportunisticPrefix`.
- Search the installed assemblies for `JobDefOf.CutPlantDesignated` equality checks. Any consumer of that check will treat the new def differently, so list each one as accepted or handled.

### 7. Save/load identity of C
- If realized blockers are saved Things with stable load IDs that survive growth re-realization, a Thing target is fine.
- If blockers are regenerated or replaced as the plant grows, a Thing reference in C goes null on load and churns during growth. In that case:
  - store C as a **cell**;
  - scan with `PotentialWorkCellsGlobal` and `JobOnCell`;
  - resolve the owner through the claims kernel.
- `GotoThing`, `FailOnDespawnedOrNull` and `CanReachImmediate` all accept cell targets.

### 8. Accepted cosmetic residue
The effecter, progress bar and `rotateToFace` stay on A, so they appear at the root behind the wall. State this explicitly. Do not claim it as art or feel work.

## Negative and positive controls (retain raw logs)

| # | Case | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Ordinary plant, vanilla cut and harvest | Same toil count and end-condition count as unpatched; wrapper takes the A branch |
| 2 | Huge plant with reachable root | Vanilla WorkGiver takes it; new WorkGiver is not reached |
| 3 | Harvest designation only, or no designation | New WorkGiver returns null |
| 4 | Plant forbidden; root outside the pawn's area | null |
| 5 | Ideology-unwilling pawn, normal and forced | null |
| 6 | Burning; PreventCutting / indestructible; gravship-protected | null |
| 7 | Plant-cutting work disabled or pawn incapable | No job |
| 8 | Two colonists at different blockers of one plant | One reservation on the plant, one job; the second pawn gets nothing |
| 9 | C owned only by a different plant | Fails at goto; no work, yield or designation change |
| 10 | C despawned or re-realized mid-walk and mid-work; setting turned off mid-job | Incompletable; plant and designation intact; no exception |
| 11 | Save/load mid-goto and mid-work; load with C invalidated | Resumes on C, or fails cleanly with no index or toil errors |
| 12 | Forced IL mismatch | Not patched, logged once, new WorkGiver inert, vanilla intact |
| 13 | Parity with a reachable-root cut of the same plant | Same yield and XP, same destruction mode, `PlantCollected` called, plant and all owned blockers gone, designation cleared |
| 14 | Shared blocker with two owners; cut one plant | Blocker persists while the other claim remains |
| 15 | Demo | Growth seals the occupied workshop doorway; a real colonist cuts via a blocker; door access is restored (reachability check before and after) |

For control 13, the ticks should satisfy `harvestWork / (PlantWorkSpeed × Lerp(3.3, 1, growth))`. Growth continues during the cut, as it does in vanilla, so compare within a tolerance or record the growth value at each tick.

If you cannot obtain the driver instance safely, or keep the toil count invariant, fall back to a subclass of `JobDriver_PlantCut_Designated` with a fully owned `MakeNewToils`. Its cut toil should call the vanilla static `WorkDonePerTick` and vanilla `PlantCollected`/yield helpers, not copy them. Do not post-process the base toils by editing `endConditions`. Those entries are anonymous closures, and you cannot reliably tell which one is the touch check.

# Independent design calls and implementation choices

Initial tools-disabled Opus design: preserve the existing door (engine has one edifice per cell; spawning a blocker would wipe it), delete approach/connectivity/root-access exceptions, and permit a real inside cutter to work from an owned trunk when its root is enclosed.

A second consultation used an incorrectly decoded TargetIndex brief. It is retained as invalid input, not adopted as independent evidence. Installed enum metadata proved None=0, A=1, B=2, C=3. Ordinary root-reachable cuts and all harvests remain vanilla.

The engine field-consumer metadata audit scans 90,840 methods. CutPlantDesignated is referenced only by WorkGiver_PlantsCut.JobOnThing and PostProcessedGerund. Contacts enumerate all claimants, not only the primary display owner.

Production fixture adapter OrderCut creates the job through the registered custom giver and TryTakeOrderedJobPrioritizedWork; it advances no ticks or work. CutState is read-only. Actual execution is governed game ticks, including in-progress save/reload and exact work/target comparison. Effects/progress still face the root; no visual/feel claim.
EOF"

def stage_build(csproj, config="Release", extra=(), extra_dirs=(), copy_back_dirs=(),
                stage_name=None, dry_run=False):
    """Stage csproj (+ what it references, + extra_dirs) on D:, build, copy outputs back.

    Returns (rc, record). Outputs copied back: every DLL/.srchash the build wrote under an
    Assemblies/ dir, plus every file the build wrote under copy_back_dirs (repo-relative).
    Callers that need a staged Windows path for a repo dir use staged_win(record, repo_dir).
    """
    csproj = os.path.realpath(csproj)
    rel_proj = os.path.relpath(csproj, ROOT)
    parts = rel_proj.split(os.sep)                       # src/<Tier>/<Mod>/Source/...
    mod = stage_name or (parts[2] if len(parts) > 3 else os.path.splitext(parts[-1])[0])
    stage = os.path.join(BUILD_ROOT, re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9_.-]", "_", mod))
    dirs = minimal(needed_dirs(csproj) | {os.path.realpath(d) for d in extra_dirs})
    print("staging %s -> %s" % (rel_proj, win(stage) if os.path.isdir(BUILD_ROOT) else stage))
    for d in dirs:
        print("  %s/" % os.path.relpath(d, ROOT))
    record = {"csproj": rel_proj, "stage": stage, "outputs": []}
    if dry_run:
        return 0, record
    os.makedirs(stage, exist_ok=True)
    """Move the clock by ONE chunk of `ticks` (WATCH_WAIT_WIRE_SMALL_STEPS): through jawa/safe_advance (paused,
    <=60-tick sub-steps inside a frame budget, stopped by the vitals latch) when the companion has it, else the
    legacy rimworld/step_game_ticks. Returns the ticks the tool says it executed (None on the legacy path: callers
    measure ticksGame themselves). Raises GovernorStop when safe_advance did not finish."""
    ticks = int(ticks)
    if ticks <= 0:
        return 0
    if not has_safe_advance(session):
        session.call("rimworld/step_game_ticks", ticks=ticks, pauseFirst=bool(pause_first))
        return None
    r = _unwrap(session.call(SAFE_ADVANCE, ticks=ticks, stopOn=stop_on, timeException=bool(time_exception),
                             timeoutMs=max(60000, ticks * 100)))
    done, resumes = 0, 0
    why = resumable_stop(r)
    while why and resumes < BENIGN_RESUME_MAX and ticks - done - int(r.get("executed") or 0) > 0:
        resumes += 1
        done += int(r.get("executed") or 0)
        BENIGN_STOPS.append({"detail": (r.get("stopBy") or {}).get("detail"), "executedBeforeStop": done, "why": why,
                             "subjectId": (r.get("stopBy") or {}).get("subjectId"),
                             "utc": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime())})
        rest = ticks - done
        r = _unwrap(session.call(SAFE_ADVANCE, ticks=rest, stopOn=stop_on, timeException=bool(time_exception),
                                 timeoutMs=max(60000, rest * 100)))
        why = resumable_stop(r)
    if why and ticks - done - int(r.get("executed") or 0) <= 0:
        # TESTENV_SWEPT_BRUISE_REPAIR_SLIPS_ITS_PASS (L1 2026-10-15): a resumable stop latched on the chunk's LAST tick
        # ("stopped after 10 of 10") leaves nothing to resume, and used to fall through to GovernorStop although the
        # stop was declared. The chunk is complete: note the stop like any other resumed one and finish.
        done += int(r.get("executed") or 0)
        BENIGN_STOPS.append({"detail": (r.get("stopBy") or {}).get("detail"), "executedBeforeStop": done, "why": why,
                             "subjectId": (r.get("stopBy") or {}).get("subjectId"),
                             "utc": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime())})
        r = dict(r, state="done", executed=0)
    if done and r.get("state") == "done":
        r = dict(r, executed=done + int(r.get("executed") or 0))
    if r.get("state") == "running":

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Start, stop and query the test-centre RimWorld on SteveDesktop. Runs in SteveDesktop's WSL
# (from Archmagi: ssh mandrake@stevedesktop-wsl ~/rm/runner/infrastructure/stevedesktop/rw_game.sh up).
#
#   rw_game.sh status         running? pid, session, bridge port from Player.log
#   rw_game.sh up [--wait]    start the game unless running; --wait blocks until the bridge
#                             announces its port in a Player.log written after the launch (max 600 s)
#   rw_game.sh down           graceful taskkill, then /F after 90 s
#   rw_game.sh init           renew the test companion profile; seed Prefs.xml if it lacks
#                             runInBackground True (game must be stopped for that half)
#
# Every verb acts on one game: RM_GAME_INSTANCE=b rw_game.sh down stops b and only b; nothing set is
# game a, as ever (src/RimMandrake/Utils/game_instance.py finds a game by its command line and stops
# it by pid). A named game's `up` starts it directly, its `init` seeds it even with game a up.
#
# STEVEDESKTOP_LAUNCH_WIRE_DESKTOP_SESSION (2026-10-25). Why it looks like this:
#  - The game on SteveDesktop is ours outright (owner, 2026-10-25: "Steve no longer plays
#    Rimworld ... this game is ours to play with"). It runs with its normal save-data folder
#    (sjlewis's LocalLow), so ModsConfig.xml, Prefs.xml and Saves there belong to the runner.
#  - The game is started by running RimWorldWin64.exe directly; Steam must be running, and `up`
#    starts it (logged in by its remembered account) when it is not.
#  - powershell.exe is reached by its full /mnt/c path: a Tailscale SSH session has no Windows
#    dirs on PATH. Started from WSL interop, the process lands in session 1 (the logged-in
#    desktop), which is where a Unity game must run; from Windows OpenSSH it would land in
#    session 0 with no display.
#  - Paths come from testcentre_env.sh (RM_STEAMAPPS, RM_GAME_USERDATA, RM_GAME_LOGDIR).
set -uo pipefail
HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
[ -n "${RM_STEAMAPPS:-}" ] || . "$HERE/testcentre_env.sh"
GI="$HERE/../../src/RimMandrake/Utils/game_instance.py"
NAMED=
case "${RM_GAME_INSTANCE:-a}" in
    a|A) ;;
    *) _env=$(python3 "$GI" env) || exit 2; eval "$_env"; NAMED=$RM_GAME_INSTANCE ;;   # after testcentre_env.sh: b's folders win
esac
PS=$(command -v powershell.exe || echo /mnt/c/Windows/System32/WindowsPowerShell/v1.0/powershell.exe)
winpath() { echo "$1" | sed -E 's#^/mnt/([a-z])/#\U\1:/#; s#/#\\#g'; }
GAME_WSL="$RM_STEAMAPPS/common/RimWorld"
EXE_WIN=$(winpath "$GAME_WSL/RimWorldWin64.exe")
DIR_WIN=$(winpath "$GAME_WSL")
DATA_WIN=$(winpath "$RM_GAME_USERDATA")
STEAM_EXE_WIN=$(winpath "$(dirname "$RM_STEAMAPPS")")\\steam.exe
LOG="$RM_GAME_LOGDIR/Player.log"

ps_q() { "$PS" -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command "\$ProgressPreference='SilentlyContinue'; $1" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\r'; }
pid_of() { python3 "$GI" pid; }   # this game's pid, nothing when it is down, non-zero when the list could not be read
gone() { local p; p=$(pid_of) && [ -z "$p" ]; }
port_in_log() { [ -f "$LOG" ] && grep -a -o '\[RimBridge\].*on port *[0-9]*' "$LOG" | tail -1 | grep -o '[0-9]*$'; }

status() {
    local pid; pid=$(pid_of) || return 2
    if [ -n "$pid" ]; then
        local info; info=$(ps_q "\$p=Get-Process -Id $pid; '{0} session={1} started={2:yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss} age_s={3}' -f \$p.Id,\$p.SessionId,\$p.StartTime,[int]((Get-Date)-\$p.StartTime).TotalSeconds")
        local args; args=$(ps_q "(Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter 'ProcessId=$pid').CommandLine")
        echo "running pid=$info"
        echo "  cmdline: $args"
        echo "  bridge port in Player.log: $(port_in_log || echo none)"
        return 0
    fi
    echo "stopped"
    return 3
}

steam_pid() { ps_q "(Get-Process steam -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -First 1).Id"; }
# Steam normally runs from the autologon (Run Steam when my computer starts). If it is not
# running, start it: with a remembered login it signs in by itself. The Steam install is
# taken as the folder above RM_STEAMAPPS; if steam.exe is not there, the registry's SteamExe.
steam_up() {
    [ -n "$(steam_pid)" ] && return 0
    local exe="$STEAM_EXE_WIN"
    [ -f "$(dirname "$RM_STEAMAPPS")/steam.exe" ] || exe=$(ps_q "(Get-ItemProperty 'HKCU:\\Software\\Valve\\Steam').SteamExe")
    [ -n "$exe" ] || { echo "REFUSED: Steam is not running and steam.exe was not found"; return 2; }
    echo "Steam not running: starting $exe -silent"
    ps_q "Start-Process -FilePath '$exe' -ArgumentList '-silent'"
    for _ in $(seq 24); do sleep 5; [ -n "$(steam_pid)" ] && { sleep 20; echo "Steam up (pid $(steam_pid))"; return 0; }; done
    echo "FAILED: Steam did not start within 120 s"; return 2
}

up() {
    local pid; pid=$(pid_of) || { echo "REFUSED: the game list could not be read; not starting a game on a guess"; return 2; }
    if [ -n "$pid" ]; then echo "already running (pid $pid)"; status; return 0; fi
    steam_up || return 2
    if [ -n "$NAMED" ]; then python3 "$GI" launch ${1:+"$1"}; return $?; fi
    local t0; t0=$(date +%s)
    ps_q "Start-Process -FilePath '$EXE_WIN' -WorkingDirectory '$DIR_WIN'"
    sleep 5
    pid=$(pid_of)
    [ -n "$pid" ] || { echo "FAILED: no RimWorldWin64 process 5 s after Start-Process"; return 1; }
    echo "started pid $pid"
    [ "${1:-}" = --wait ] || return 0
    while [ $(( $(date +%s) - t0 )) -lt 600 ]; do
        if [ -f "$LOG" ] && [ "$(stat -c %Y "$LOG")" -ge "$t0" ] && port_in_log >/dev/null; then
            echo "bridge up on port $(port_in_log) after $(( $(date +%s) - t0 )) s"; return 0
        fi
        [ -n "$(pid_of)" ] || { echo "FAILED: game exited during load; tail of Player.log:"; tail -n 15 "$LOG"; return 1; }
        sleep 5
    done
    echo "TIMEOUT: no bridge port in a fresh Player.log after 600 s"; return 1
}

# A fresh or reset save-data folder lacks two files that modcheck run refuses without
# (found on the first remote run, 2026-10-25):
#  - JawaBench/companion_profile.json: with none the companion reports profile 'campaign'
#    and ensure_test_profile raises. Every save in this folder is the runner's (the game is
#    ours, owner 2026-10-25), so 'test' is true; the expiry is renewed to 30 days ahead on
#    every init.
#  - Config/Prefs.xml with runInBackground True: game_focus.preflight refuses
#    (FocusRefused, runInBackground UNREADABLE) without it. The game writes Prefs.xml on a
#    clean exit only, and rewrites it from memory then, so it can be seeded only while the
#    game is stopped. Prefs.template.xml is Archmagi's Prefs minus the screen size.
init() {
    if [ -n "$NAMED" ]; then python3 "$GI" prepare; return $?; fi
    mkdir -p "$RM_GAME_USERDATA/JawaBench" "$RM_GAME_USERDATA/Config"
    local exp; exp=$(date -u -d '+30 days' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    local esc; esc=$(printf '%s' "$DATA_WIN" | sed 's/\\/\\\\/g')   # JSON-escape the backslashes
    cat > "$RM_GAME_USERDATA/JawaBench/companion_profile.json" <<EOF
{
  "profile": "test",
  "expiresUtc": "$exp",
  "campaignSaves": "",
  "why": "SteveDesktop test centre: the game and every save in $esc are the runner's (rw_game.sh init)"
}
EOF
    echo "companion profile: test until $exp"
    local prefs="$RM_GAME_USERDATA/Config/Prefs.xml"
    if grep -q '<runInBackground>True</runInBackground>' "$prefs" 2>/dev/null; then
        echo "Prefs.xml: runInBackground True"; return 0
    fi
    [ -z "$(pid_of)" ] || { echo "REFUSED: Prefs.xml lacks runInBackground True and the game is running (it would overwrite the fix on exit); run down, then init"; return 2; }
    [ -f "$prefs" ] && cp "$prefs" "$prefs.pre-init" && echo "Prefs.xml: old copy kept as Prefs.xml.pre-init"
    cp "$HERE/Prefs.template.xml" "$prefs"
    echo "Prefs.xml: seeded from Prefs.template.xml"
}

down() {
    local pid; pid=$(pid_of) || { echo "REFUSED: the game list could not be read; nothing stopped"; return 2; }
    [ -n "$pid" ] || { echo "already stopped"; return 0; }
    python3 "$GI" stop "$pid" >/dev/null
    for _ in $(seq 18); do sleep 5; gone && { echo "stopped (graceful)"; return 0; }; done
    python3 "$GI" stop "$pid" --force >/dev/null; sleep 3

## 1. Current data model and lifecycle

### 1.1 What it is for

Measured ground-contact masks follow the actual plant picture and growth. One impassable partial-cover edifice
per realized contact cell makes the trunk solid while leaving the canopy open. The root remains its plant Thing;
no blocker is spawned over it. Per-species masks and current variant identity come from the generated

### 1.2 Shared claims and physical cells

`ClaimLedger` maps each cell to all claiming owner IDs. The map component holds one physical blocker per realized
cell. The lowest claimant is its display/damage owner; cutting checks all claimants. Removing one plant releases
only its claims, and a shared cell remains solid until its last claimant is removed.

### 1.3 Refresh and load

Registration queues the owner. Growth/harvest/signature changes and settings generations trigger a sliced refresh;
geometry, old claims, removals and additions resume across ticks. Reconcile indexes all physical blockers, drops
duplicates and unclaimed cells, rebuilds claims from spawned plants and attempts pending placement. Runtime death
queues bounded cleanup instead of walking and relabeling the whole map synchronously.

### 1.4 Placement and cutting

Planner accepts exactly passable unprotected cells without pawns or items. Protection includes the entire pawn
body, existing buildings (including doors), blueprints, frames, interactions, trees, other giants and indestructibles.
Ordinary items move only to valid free destinations outside every claim when pushing is enabled; quest items remain
pending. Failed placement never permits wiping. Door approaches have no special protection; no connectivity or
root-access flood remains. A colonist can cut an enclosed root by working from an owned realized trunk cell through

All loaded maps share `WorkUnitsPerTick = 200000` logical units; a map receives a child share. Each tick visits at

# BROADEN: trunk-doors live script and inputs

I ran nothing. Everything below comes from reading the frozen text. Nothing here counts as a pass.

## The main finding: the geometry makes the access question unanswerable

Look at the cells in `scenario()`:

- The root sits at (100,100). Seven of its neighbours are walls; the only open one is (100,101).
- (100,101) is the cell just outside the door. Its eight neighbours are:
  - the root (100,100),
  - four root-ring walls: (99,100), (101,100), (99,101), (101,101),
  - two workshop walls: (99,102), (101,102),
  - the door itself (100,102).
- So {(100,101), (100,100)} is a walled pocket. The workshop's only exit leads into it. The workshop is sealed by walls before any plant exists.

This has four consequences:

1. **The baseline check should fail.** If the walls are complete, `require(self.reach(cutter, 100, 97), 'SITE: workshop already inaccessible')` should fail. The error would be labelled SITE, but it is a HARNESS geometry fault. If that check has ever passed, the walls or the reach probe were not what the script assumes (for example, unbuilt blueprints, or `order_pawn.canReach` not answering a path question). Every later result would then be unfounded.
2. **"Sealed" means nothing here.** `sealed = not reach(...)` would be true with or without a blocker.
3. **"Access restored" cannot pass honestly.** Removing the plant and blocker still leaves the ring walls. A pass would point to a probe or build defect, not to working cutting.
4. **The old-build reproduction would not discriminate.** The old access-preserving build would stop at the same SITE precondition, before the `MOD: growth did not seal…` assertion. The fact that "the old build fails" would therefore show nothing about the mod. A valid reproduction must fail at exactly that MOD assertion, with recorded values `blockers == []` and `access == True`. A failure at any earlier step is not a reproduction.

This is also geometrically unavoidable with a one-cell contact. You cannot have the root's only touch cell be the door approach while that approach also has another route outside. The root ring has to open, and the trunk footprint must be shown to claim every opened cell. Alternatively, move the root so its multi-cell footprint covers the approach. In either case the chokepoint has to be proven, not assumed (Control 1).

## Messy cases a real player would hit that these inputs miss

**Designation and orders**
- The player drags the cut designation over the visible trunk cells rather than the root cell. The script designates only `100,100,1,1`.
- The player uses Harvest instead of Cut on a harvestable giant. `JobOnThing` accepts only `CutPlantDesignated`, so a harvest-designated enclosed root is silently never worked.
- The player right-clicks the trunk to prioritize cutting. Nothing shows the float menu offers this for a `Building_TrunkBlocker`.
- **Natural pickup is never exercised.** `OrderCut` uses `forced=true` and `TryTakeOrderedJobPrioritizedWork`. That is not a colonist picking the job up through the think tree. The forced and unforced paths can differ in vanilla gates such as area and forbidden checks, and the `playerForced` flag.

**Pawns**
- A pawn stands on (100,101) or in the doorway at the moment of realization: idle, sleeping, downed, or mid-path. Only a drafted guard far away is tested.
- Every colonist inside is incapable of PlantCutting, or the only capable cutter is outside.
- The cutter's allowed area excludes the trunk cell or the door, or the door is forbidden.

**Multiple plants and aftermath**
- Two Nogtyl footprints claim the same approach. `CutOwners` loops over owners, but nothing shows that cutting one plant leaves the other's blocker correctly attributed.
- The yield spawns inside an enclosed pocket and cannot be hauled.
- A sapling, stump or spreading neighbour re-seals the door right after the cut.
- The plant dies some other way (fire, blight, an animal eating it, a debug-free raid). Nothing checks that its blockers are cleaned up.
- Settings are toggled off while sealed, then the game is saved and reloaded. Or it is reloaded while sealed but before any designation.

**Untested scope**
- The statement requires preserving the **indestructible and gravship constraints**, with focused controls. The script has no control for either: no blocker against a non-destroyable Thing, and none on or near gravship substructure. That requirement is untested, not preserved.

**Weak negative probes**
- The `no_designation_probe` and the second-cutter reservation probe accept `job is None` for *any* reason.
- The second pawn is spawned **drafted** and never given a PlantCutting priority. Its `None` could come from either of those rather than from the reservation.

## Control 1: prove the chokepoint with a removable plain wall (geometry versus mod)

Before staging the plant, using the same fixture IDs:

| Step | Action | Expected | If not |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1a | Revised geometry with the root ring opened as designed; no plant, no blocker | `reach(cutter, 100, 97) == True`; path census shows no blocker | HARNESS (geometry), not SITE |
| 1b | Build a plain wall (player faction, completed, not a blueprint; confirm the def is `Wall`, not a frame) on **every** cell the mod will claim. Get that list from `DebugCellState` at a pre-measured growth, not from the script's guess. | `reach == False` | Another route exists, so "sealed" is meaningless: HARNESS |
| 1c | Destroy those walls and confirm the census is empty | `reach == True` again | HARNESS or SITE (probe is stateful) |
| 2 | Natural growth, as now | Blockers on exactly the claimed cell set from 1b; `reach == False`; door ID and HP unchanged | Blockers present but `reach == True`: HARNESS (1b list wrong). No blockers, plant `oldEnough=True`: **MOD** (old access-preserving behaviour) |
| 3 | After the real cut | Plant ID absent; zero blockers in the bounded rect; `reach == True`; yield stack reachable from the cutter | `reach == False` with zero blockers: HARNESS. Blockers remain: **MOD** |

Expected old-build signature: it passes 1a, 1b and 1c, then fails at step 2 with `blockers == []` and `access == True`. The raw record should mark that failure site explicitly, for example as `rec['failure_stage'] = 'MOD_seal'`. Any other failure stage means the reproduction is invalid.

## Control 2: unforced natural pickup, with a negative that differs by one gate

**Positive.** Use an undrafted inside cutter with PlantCutting at priority 1, all other work types disabled, CutPlant designated by dragging over the **trunk cells and root**, and no `OrderCut`.
- Expected within a bounded tick budget, recorded as `CutState` samples: `current == RM_CutHugePlantFromTrunk`, `plant == plant_id`, `contact == blocker_id`, and `job.playerForced == False`. That last field needs to be added to `CutState`.
- If no job starts and the probe shows designation present, `canReach=True` and `canReserve=True`: **MOD** (scanner or think-tree integration).
- If no job starts and the pawn is drafted, missing the priority, or in a mental state: HARNESS.

**Matched negative.** Start a second undrafted pawn with the same priority while the first cutter holds the job. The probe must show all of the following:
- designation present,
- `canReach == True` to the blocker,
- `canReserve == False`,
- `job == None`.

Interpretation:
- `job == None` with any other gate false means the control is invalid (HARNESS).
- Any job at all is a **MOD** reservation bypass.

Apply the same field-level rule to the no-designation probe. All gates other than designation must be true; otherwise its `None` proves nothing.

## Status

No live acceptance exists. Before any result from `trunk_doors_live.py` is treated as evidence, two things need settling:

- The geometry defect means past or future passes need raw review of the build census and reach rows.
- Old-build failures need the stage attribution from Control 1.

        require(result.get('truncated') == 0 and result.get('returned') == len(result.get('pawns', [])), 'incomplete pawn census')
        return result['pawns']

    def reach(self, pawn, x, z):
        result = self.call('jawa/order_pawn', allow=True, pawnId=pawn, x=x, z=z, pathEndMode='oncell',
                           waitTicks=0, unpause=False, draft=True)
        self.call('jawa/stop_job', pawnId=pawn, mode='stopall')
        rows = result.get('pawns', [])
        require(len(rows) == 1 and result.get('ticksElapsed') == 0 and rows[0]['start'] == rows[0]['end'], 'invalid paused path read')
        require(type(rows[0].get('canReach')) is bool, 'path answer missing')
        return rows[0]['canReach']

    def spawn_pawn(self, x, z):
        rows = self.call('jawa/spawn_pawn', kindDef='Colonist', x=x, z=z, faction='player', count=1, xenotype='Baseliner')['pawns']
        require(len(rows) == 1, 'wrong spawn cardinality')
        pid = rows[0]['id']
        self.rec['fixture_ids'].append(pid)
        C.declare_fixture(pid)
        self.call('jawa/set_draft', pawnId=pid, drafted=True)
        return pid

    def stage_plant(self, x, z, growth=0.2499):
        result = self.call('jawa/artboard_stage', phase='subjects', pause=True, killHostiles=False,
                           ops='id=plant|kind=plant|x=%d|z=%d|def=%s|growth=%.7f' % (x, z, PLANT, growth))
        rows = result.get('ops', [])
        require(len(rows) == 1 and rows[0].get('ok') and abs(float(rows[0]['readBack']['growth'])-growth) < 0.000001, 'plant initial growth not staged exactly')
        plants = self.things(PLANT, '%d,%d,1,1' % (x, z))
        require(len(plants) == 1, 'plant identity missing')
        return plants[0]['id']

    def identity(self, tid):
        rows = [t for t in self.things() if t['id'] == tid]
        require(len(rows) == 1, 'lost Thing '+tid)
        return rows[0]

    def scenario(self, tx):
        require(not self.pawns(), 'SITE: target rectangle already contains pawns; refuse clearing')
        self.call('jawa/set_roof_batch', ops='None:'+RECT)
        self.call('jawa/destroy_batch', categories='All', rects=RECT)
        require(not self.things(), 'SITE: bounded clear left objects')
        self.call('jawa/set_terrain_batch', ops='Soil:'+RECT)
        for field, value in dict(giantPlantsEnabled=True, plantTrunkEnabled=True, plantTrunkScale=1, plantItemPushEnabled=False).items():
            self.setting(field, value)
        self.sc('RefreshAllMaps')
        # A real workshop with one southern door. The root outside is surrounded
        # on six adjacent cells by existing walls; its only open touch
        # cell is the doorway approach, which is genuine Nogtyl contact after growth.
        walls = {(x, z) for x in range(95, 106) for z in (102, 111)} | {(x, z) for x in (95, 105) for z in range(103, 111)}
        walls.remove((100, 102))
        walls |= {(99, 99), (100, 99), (101, 99), (99, 100), (101, 100), (101, 101)}
        self.call('jawa/build_batch', ops=';'.join('Wall:%d,%d' % p for p in sorted(walls)), stuff='WoodLog', faction='player')
        self.call('jawa/build_batch', ops='Door:100,102;TableStonecutter:98,108', stuff='WoodLog', faction='player')
        door = self.things('Door', '100,102,1,1')
        bench = self.things('TableStonecutter', '96,106,5,5')
        require(len(door) == len(bench) == 1, 'workshop door/bench not built')
        self.rec['door_before'], self.rec['bench_before'] = door[0], bench[0]
        cutter = None
        self.rec['cutter_candidates'] = []
        for attempt in range(6):
            pid = self.spawn_pawn(100+attempt % 2, 107+attempt // 2)
            priority = self.call('jawa/set_work_priority', allow=True, pawnId=pid, workType='PlantCutting', priority=1)
            self.rec['cutter_candidates'].append(dict(pawn=pid, priority=priority))
            if priority.get('success') is True and int(priority.get('readBack', 0)) > 0:
                cutter = pid
                break
        require(cutter is not None, 'SITE: bounded Baseliner candidates have no capable PlantCutting worker')
        self.rec['cutter'] = cutter
        self.rec['failure_stage'] = 'HARNESS_baseline_geometry'
        require(self.reach(cutter, 100, 97), 'HARNESS: workshop already inaccessible')
        # These are the two open root-touch cells; both are measured Nogtyl
        # contact after the threshold. Closing them must seal this exact room.
        self.rec['geometry_obstruction_cells'] = [[99, 101], [100, 101]]
        self.call('jawa/build_batch', ops='Wall:99,101;Wall:100,101', stuff='WoodLog', faction='player')
        obstruction = self.things('Wall', '99,101,2,1')
        self.rec['failure_stage'] = 'HARNESS_planted_obstruction'
        require(len(obstruction) == 2 and not self.reach(cutter, 100, 97), 'HARNESS: planted walls do not seal chokepoint')
        self.call('jawa/destroy_batch', categories='Buildings', rects='99,101,2,1')
        require(not self.things(None, '99,101,2,1') and self.reach(cutter, 100, 97), 'HARNESS: removing control walls did not restore route')
        self.rec['geometry_control'] = dict(blocked=obstruction, restored_access=True)
        plant = self.stage_plant(100, 100)
        self.rec['plant_id'] = plant
        young = self.sc('DebugPlantState', 'current|100,100')
        require(kv(young).get('oldEnough') == 'False' and kv(young).get('desired') == '0' and kv(young).get('blockingSupported') == 'True' and kv(young).get('blocking') == 'True', 'HARNESS: not a supported enabled young unblocked plant')
        require(not self.things(BLOCKER, '96,96,9,6') and self.reach(cutter, 100, 97), 'young plant already seals access')
        self.rec['young_state'] = young
        samples = []
        for _ in range(6):
            self.ticks(2000)
            state = self.sc('DebugPlantState', 'current|100,100')
            samples.append(dict(state=state, things=self.things(BLOCKER, '96,96,9,6')))
            if kv(state).get('oldEnough') == 'True' and int(kv(state).get('claimed', 0)) > 0:
                break
        self.rec['growth_samples'] = samples
        require(samples and kv(samples[-1]['state']).get('oldEnough') == 'True' and int(kv(samples[-1]['state']).get('desired', 0)) > 0 and int(kv(samples[-1]['state']).get('claimed', 0)) > 0, 'SITE: plant did not naturally grow claimed contacts')
        require(float(kv(samples[-1]['state'])['growth']) > 0.2499, 'no measured natural growth')
        self.ticks(500)
        blockers = self.things(BLOCKER, '100,101,1,1')
        sealed = not self.reach(cutter, 100, 97)
        self.rec['sealed'] = dict(blockers=blockers, access=not sealed, state=self.sc('DebugPlantState', 'current|100,100'))
        self.rec['doorway_claims'] = self.claimed_cells([(99, 101), (100, 101)])
        self.rec['failure_stage'] = 'MOD_seal'
        require(sealed and len(blockers) == 1, 'MOD: growth did not seal workshop doorway (old access-preserving behavior)')
        require(len(self.things(BLOCKER, '99,101,1,1')) == 1, 'MOD: second open root-touch cell did not fill')
        require(self.identity(door[0]['id']) == door[0], 'growth changed door identity/HP')
        # Standard root work is explicitly unable to reach it. The replacement
        # giver must permit touching this owned blocker, not silently leave a gap.
        absent = self.call('jawa/workgiver_probe', pawn=cutter, thing=blockers[0]['id'], workGiver=CUT)
        require(absent['gates']['canReach'] is True and absent['gates']['workActive'] is True and absent.get('job') is None,
                'missing-designation negative has another false scan gate')
        self.rec['no_designation_probe'] = absent
        self.call('jawa/designate_batch', action='add', designation='CutPlant', rect='100,100,1,1')
        root_probe = self.call('jawa/workgiver_probe', pawn=cutter, thing=plant, workGiver='PlantsCut')
        require(root_probe['gates']['canReachTouchDeadly'] is False, 'root was deliberately left reachable')
        probe = self.call('jawa/workgiver_probe', pawn=cutter, thing=blockers[0]['id'], workGiver=CUT)
        self.rec['cut_probes'] = dict(root=root_probe, trunk=probe)
        require(probe['gates']['canReach'] is True and probe['gates']['canReserve'] is True and probe.get('job', {}).get('def') == CUT,
                'trunk cutting giver did not produce a reachable/reservable real job')
        self.rec['failure_stage'] = 'MOD_natural_cut_pickup'
        prepared = self.sc('PrepareCutter', cutter, 'RimMandrake.HugeThings.TrunkDoorValidationHooks')
        self.rec['cutter_prepared'] = prepared
        second = None
        self.rec['second_candidates'] = []
        for attempt in range(6):
            pid = self.spawn_pawn(101+attempt % 2, 107+attempt // 2)
            priority = self.call('jawa/set_work_priority', allow=True, pawnId=pid, workType='PlantCutting', priority=1)
            self.rec['second_candidates'].append(dict(pawn=pid, priority=priority))
            if priority.get('success') is True and int(priority.get('readBack', 0)) > 0:
                second = pid
                break
        require(second is not None, 'HARNESS: no capable second reservation worker')
        self.sc('PrepareCutter', second, 'RimMandrake.HugeThings.TrunkDoorValidationHooks')
        self.call('jawa/set_draft', pawnId=second, drafted=False)
        second_positive = self.call('jawa/workgiver_probe', pawn=second, thing=blockers[0]['id'], workGiver=CUT)
        require(second_positive['gates']['canReach'] is True and second_positive['gates']['workActive'] is True and
                second_positive.get('job', {}).get('def') == CUT, 'second cutter has no matched unreserved positive')
        self.rec['second_unreserved_positive'] = second_positive
        self.call('jawa/set_draft', pawnId=second, drafted=True)
        # No OrderCut or ordered_job: only a cut designation and normal work AI.
        self.call('jawa/set_draft', pawnId=cutter, drafted=False)
        self.call('jawa/stop_job', pawnId=cutter, mode='stopall')
        self.rec['pickup_samples'] = []
        for _ in range(25):
            self.ticks(20)
            state = self.sc('CutState', cutter, 'RimMandrake.HugeThings.TrunkDoorValidationHooks')
            self.rec['pickup_samples'].append(state)
            if kv(state).get('current') == CUT:
                break
        require(kv(state).get('current') == CUT and kv(state).get('forced') == 'False' and kv(state).get('plant') == plant
                and kv(state).get('contact') == blockers[0]['id'], 'unforced natural worker pickup did not start correct trunk job')
        self.rec['cut_order'] = state
        # A second capable, undrafted cutter can reach the trunk but the plant is
        # reserved. Probe both the scan target and the actual reservation target.
        self.call('jawa/set_draft', pawnId=second, drafted=False)
        reservation = self.call('jawa/workgiver_probe', pawn=second, thing=blockers[0]['id'], workGiver=CUT)
        root_reservation = self.call('jawa/workgiver_probe', pawn=second, thing=plant, workGiver='PlantsCut')
        require(reservation['gates']['canReach'] is True and reservation['gates']['workActive'] is True and
                root_reservation['gates']['canReserve'] is False and reservation.get('job') is None,
                'matched reservation negative has another false gate or bypassed root reservation')
        self.rec['reservation_control'] = dict(trunk=reservation, root=root_reservation)
        self.call('jawa/set_draft', pawnId=second, drafted=True)
        self.rec['cut_work_samples'] = []
        for _ in range(20):
            self.ticks(20)
            state = self.sc('CutState', cutter, 'RimMandrake.HugeThings.TrunkDoorValidationHooks')
            self.rec['cut_work_samples'].append(state)
            require(kv(state).get('current') == CUT, 'cutting job exited before measured work')
            if float(kv(state)['work']) > 0:
                break
        require(float(kv(state)['work']) > 0 and any(t['id'] == plant for t in self.things(PLANT)), 'no real in-progress work before cutting save')
        work_before_save = state
        occupied = 'CODEX_TrunkDoors_Cutting_'+uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]
        self.rec['cut_save'] = T.save_site(self.call, occupied, G.SAVES)
        self.rec['cut_reload'] = T.load_site(self.call, 'calm', name=occupied, check=False, map_controls=('modal_broker',))
        require(self.rec['cut_reload']['verified'], 'cutting snapshot did not reload')
        H.quiet_world(T.call_session(self.call), tx, wild_spawner=False, log_raids=False)
        self.rec['cut_job_after_reload'] = self.sc('CutState', cutter, 'RimMandrake.HugeThings.TrunkDoorValidationHooks')
        restored_work = kv(self.rec['cut_job_after_reload'])
        require(restored_work.get('current') == CUT and restored_work.get('plant') == plant and
                restored_work.get('contact') == blockers[0]['id'] and restored_work.get('work') == kv(work_before_save).get('work'),
                'cutting work/targets changed across occupied reload')
        for _ in range(30):
            self.ticks(100)
            if not any(t['id'] == plant for t in self.things(PLANT)):
                break
        require(not any(t['id'] == plant for t in self.things(PLANT)), 'actual cutting job never removed enclosed plant')
        self.call('jawa/set_draft', pawnId=cutter, drafted=True)
        self.ticks(500)
        require(not self.things(BLOCKER, '96,96,9,6'), 'plant blockers survived cutting/cleanup')
        require(self.reach(cutter, 100, 97), 'access not restored after real cutting')
        require(self.identity(door[0]['id']) == door[0] and self.identity(bench[0]['id']) == bench[0], 'cutting altered door/workshop')
        self.rec['cut_recovered'] = True
        self.rec['failure_stage'] = 'MOD_placement_controls'
        self.controls()

    def controls(self):
        # Each plant has positive free contact cells as well as the obstructed
        # one: an absent/disabled footprint cannot satisfy placement protection.
        guard = self.spawn_pawn(125, 101)
        self.call('jawa/spawn_batch', ops='Steel:140,101,17')
        item = self.things('Steel', '140,101,1,1')
        require(len(item) == 1, 'item control absent')
        self.call('jawa/build_batch', ops='Door:155,101', stuff='WoodLog', faction='player')
        door = self.things('Door', '155,101,1,1')
        require(len(door) == 1, 'protected building control absent')
        for x in (125, 140, 155, 175):
            self.stage_plant(x, 100)
        self.ticks(2000)
        self.ticks(500)
        self.rec['guarded_cell_claims'] = self.claimed_cells([(125, 101), (140, 101), (155, 101)])
        for x in (125, 140, 155):
            require(not self.things(BLOCKER, '%d,101,1,1' % x), 'placement control was overwritten')
            require(self.things(BLOCKER, '%d,98,7,6' % (x-3)), 'obstruction control has no positive free-space blocker')
        require(self.identity(item[0]['id']) == item[0], 'item moved/wiped with item push disabled')
        require(self.identity(door[0]['id']) == door[0], 'existing building wiped/changed')
        pawn_rows = [p for p in self.pawns() if p['id'] == guard]
        require(len(pawn_rows) == 1 and pawn_rows[0]['x'] == 125 and pawn_rows[0]['z'] == 101 and not pawn_rows[0].get('dead') and not pawn_rows[0].get('downed'), 'pawn placement control moved/hurt')
        self.setting('plantItemPushEnabled', True)
        self.ticks(500)
        moved = self.identity(item[0]['id'])
        require(moved['stackCount'] == item[0]['stackCount'] and (moved['x'], moved['z']) != (140, 101), 'item push lost its stack or did not move')
        require(kv(self.sc('DebugCellState', 'current|%d,%d' % (moved['x'], moved['z']))).get('claimed') == 'False', 'item pushed into another footprint')
        require(self.things(BLOCKER, '140,101,1,1'), 'cleared item cell never realized')
        self.call('jawa/order_pawn', pawnId=guard, x=125, z=105, waitTicks=0, unpause=False, draft=True)
        self.ticks(100)
        self.ticks(500)
        require(self.things(BLOCKER, '125,101,1,1'), 'vacated pawn contact never retried')
        free_before = self.things(BLOCKER, '172,98,7,6')
        require(free_before, 'free-space positive has no blockers')
        self.setting('plantTrunkEnabled', False)
        self.sc('RefreshAllMaps')
        self.ticks(500)
        require(not self.things(BLOCKER), 'disabled trunk feature left blockers')
        self.setting('plantTrunkEnabled', True)
        self.sc('RefreshAllMaps')
        self.ticks(500)
        require(self.things(BLOCKER, '172,98,7,6'), 'reenabled free-space feature did not resume')
        self.rec['controls'] = dict(pawn=guard, item=item[0], building=door[0], free_before=free_before,
                                    item_after_push=moved, vacated_pawn_retried=True, disabled=True, reenabled=True)


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument('--out', type=Path, required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    args.out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

        baseline = r.sc('Rect', RECT, PROOF)

        require(quiet.verified, 'quiet controls unreadable')
        r.rec['quiet'] = quiet.evidence
        r.scenario(tx)
        r.rec['ok'] = True
    except Exception as exc:
        r.rec['error'] = repr(exc)
    finally:
        errors = []
        if saved:
            try:
                r.rec['restore_load'] = T.load_site(r.call, 'calm', name=snapshot, check=False, map_controls=('modal_broker',))
                require(r.rec['restore_load']['verified'], 'scene-begin restoration load failed')
                restored = r.sc('Rect', RECT, PROOF)
                restored_pawns = r.pawns()
                r.rec['restored'] = dict(rectangle=restored, pawns=restored_pawns)
                require(restored == baseline and restored_pawns == baseline_pawns, 'restored rectangle/fixtures differ from exact baseline')
            except Exception as exc:
                errors.append(repr(exc))
        for field, value in r.prior.items():
            try:
                r.setting(field, value)
